# core.py
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Greeting:
    name: str
    text: str


SHOUT_SUFFIX = "!"


def greet(name: str, *, shout: bool = False) -> Greeting:
    clean = name.strip()
    if not clean:
        msg = "name must not be empty"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    text = f"Hello, {clean}"
    if shout:
        text = text.upper() + SHOUT_SUFFIX
    return Greeting(name=clean, text=text)

# cli.py
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="app")
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    hello = commands.add_parser("hello", help="greet someone")
    hello.add_argument("name")
    hello.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print JSON")
    hello.add_argument("--shout", action="store_true", help="upper-case the greeting")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        greeting = greet(str(args.name), shout=bool(args.shout))
    except ValueError as err:
        if args.json:
            sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"error": str(err)}) + "\n")
        else:
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: {err}\n")
        return 2
    sys.stdout.write((json.dumps(asdict(greeting)) if args.json else greeting.text) + "\n")
    return 0

def repo_skill_roots(cwd="."):
    """The target repo's .agents/skills: this checkout's, then the main checkout's."""
    def git(*a):
        r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cwd, *a], capture_output=True, text=True)
        return r.stdout.strip() if r.returncode == 0 else ""
    tops = [git("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel") or os.path.abspath(cwd)]
    common = git("rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir")
    if common.endswith("/.git"):
        tops.append(os.path.dirname(common))
    roots = []
    for t in tops:
        r = os.path.join(t, ".agents", "skills")
        if r not in roots:
            roots.append(r)
    return roots

Test:
# 6. Where review-host.py cannot see its live server (no /proc, as on macOS), the link holds and the old server
#    is gone: register runs in a user+mount namespace with tmpfs over /proc; `ps` (macOS-style, args joined by
#    spaces) reads the real /proc, bound aside before it is covered.
mkdir -p "$t/realproc" "$t/psbin"
cat > "$t/psbin/ps" <<'PY'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
proc = os.environ["FAKE_PS_PROC"]
for pid in filter(str.isdigit, os.listdir(proc)):
    try:
        argv = open(f"{proc}/{pid}/cmdline", "rb").read().rstrip(b"\0").split(b"\0")
        uid = os.stat(f"{proc}/{pid}").st_uid
    except OSError:
        continue
    if argv != [b""]:
        print(pid, uid, b" ".join(argv).decode(errors="replace"))
PY
chmod +x "$t/psbin/ps"
noproc() { unshare -rm sh -c 'mount --rbind /proc "$1" && mount -t tmpfs none /proc && shift && exec "$@"' sh "$t/realproc" "$@"; }
if ! noproc sh -c '! test -e /proc/self' 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "review-host: ok (no-/proc case skipped: unshare -rm cannot cover /proc here)"
else
  before="$(serve_pids)"
  page v5 "$script"
  set +e; out="$(FAKE_PS_PROC="$t/realproc" PATH="$t/psbin:$PATH" noproc "$kit/scripts/review-host" register \
    --state-dir "$state" --test --slug w65 --owner test/w65 --base HEAD docs/specs/x.spec.html 2>&1)"; rc=$?; set -e
  [[ "$rc" == 0 ]] || fail "register v5 without /proc: $out"
  [[ "$(link)" == "$first" ]] || fail "without /proc the link moved: $first -> $(link)"
  [[ "$(serve_pids)" != "$before" ]] || fail "without /proc the old server was not replaced"
  check_link v5
fi
